comparator.name: Communication Science (Communicatiewetenschap)
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target merges English Communication Science and Dutch Communicatiewetenschap registrations. The adopted OER first lists the English route; both are language versions of the same subject. Ten 6-EC units fill Year 1; eight 6-EC named courses and two restricted Social Sciences for Society choice slots fill Year 2. Year 3 has 30 EC of genuinely open approved electives, Current Media Challenges (6), Philosophy of Science (6) and an 18-EC empirical bachelor thesis. Zero-credit mentorship is excluded. Choice menus are represented as slots, not accumulated options.
components: Journalism: News and Information in a Changing World
Interpersonal Communication: The Dynamics of Everyday Interactions
Marketing Communication: The Psychology of Persuasion
Media Entertainment: The Power of Media Engagement
Media, Power and Technology: Understanding Public Debate
Health Communication: Effective Campaigns for Behavior Change
One of Beyond Gender Inequalities, Confronting Commodity Chains or Towards Better Care and Welfare; recorded as a choice slot, not all options.
One of AI & Society, Social Entrepreneurship: Creating a Sustainable World or The Human Dimension of Sustainable Development; recorded as a choice slot, not all options.
Genuinely open first-semester minor, approved elective courses, study abroad or internship; no invented specialization.

routeSelection.basis: The merged registry target names both Dutch and English registrations; the adopted OER lists the English-language track first. Select that route under the neutral official-order tie break, without reference to UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Communication, media and social research
alternatives.concept: Combines media studies, rhetorical communication, social psychology and empirical research to examine audiences, organizations and digital public life. The UCR curriculum offers related methods and perspectives but does not reproduce VU’s semester projects, specialist media data sequence or 18-EC empirical thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule integrates media, persuasion, audience psychology, organizational contexts and quantitative and qualitative methods.
progression: Six fixed four-course semesters in 2026–29; at least six advanced courses, PPD in Year 1, official workbook term availability and formal prerequisites verified. Introductory communication, media and methods generally precede advanced study.

alternatives.label: Digital media, representation and public debate
alternatives.concept: Centers media forms, digital audiences, representation and contested public messages, using communication and social research to investigate how information circulates. It develops media criticism and civic questions in greater depth while keeping VU’s communication-science core in view.
alternatives.labelReason: Additional media, language and climate-communication courses make digital and public discourse the organizing emphasis.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change: Style & Meaning, Communicating the Climate Crisis, Film & Text and Perspectives on Literary Meaning replace Research Methods & Statistics, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership and Market Research; media interpretation and public debate take the place of organizational marketing and market research.
progression: Six fixed four-course semesters in 2026–29; at least six advanced courses, PPD in Year 1, official workbook term availability and formal prerequisites verified. Introductory communication, media and methods generally precede advanced study.

candidates.label: Organizational persuasion, marketing and health communication

selection.assessment: The first schedule is the strongest broad communication science response. The second makes digital media, representation and civic messages a distinct emphasis with four consequential course changes. A third health-campaign or social-platform variant would duplicate the same communication and methods base and lack enough distinct specialist UCR courses to support a separate coherent 24-course direction.

notes.text: VU requires four communication-project courses, specialist social-media analytics, health communication, public relations, restricted social-science choices and an 18-EC empirical thesis. UCR offers a related interdisciplinary combination of media, rhetoric, psychology, business and social research, but those structured specialist requirements and thesis are not replicated.
